subject: Re: Kickoff: typology prediction for coverage planning
body:
Hi both,

Status: NEMO reproduction is complete. Our runs match the shared-task submission — the frequentist approach (per-feature estimators with typological-constraint filtering) beats the majority-class baseline comfortably on the blind test set, and per-family accuracy tracks the paper.

Beyond reproduction: Quentin added two neural comparison arms (a feature-embedding MLP and a graph-propagation model over language families). In the sparse-observation regime that matters for our product — five or fewer observed features per language — NEMO still wins; the neural arms only pull ahead past ~15 observed features, which real unknown languages rarely have.

Risk for the sweep: WALS sparsity is brutal — many features have <300 attested languages — so the full-matrix imputation confidence intervals will be wide. Oyin is adding per-feature reliability scores so the i18n consumers know which predictions to trust.

Umar
